messages:
emily: short notes from a focused sim on active-active with residency constraints. posting results + suggested runtime interfaces.
ops-bot: Simulation 2026-03-20T10:15Z complete. scenario: 2-region active-active, jitter 200-300ms, tenant set 800 (250 strict-residency). flags: consent-hint applied.
raj: top-line, any split-brain or long tail events?
emily: two recurring issues: transient write divergence when backlog >2k, and prolonged read staleness when residency blocked failover and queues grew.
zara: divergence = conflicting commits across regions? how visible to clients?
emily: yes. conflict pattern: region A preempts lease but region B had buffered mutates that committed because request acceptance checked local seq not global epoch. SDKs saw non-deterministic last-write.
tom: did you test fixes?
emily: three candidate runtime changes: (1) epoch stamping on mutates + strict epoch check at accept, (2) brief staged drain that blocks new mutates during handoff (200ms), (3) tentative-write proxy where writes return 202 + token until lease confirmed.
ops-bot: Results summary: (1) removes most divergence but adds ~80ms median accept latency. (2) reduces overlap but increases tail queueing under burst. (3) minimal latency impact but requires client reconciliation semantics and GC of tentative writes.
zara: i'm leaning to (3) as default, with (1) available for strict-residency tenants. need clear client API for tentative writes.
emily: proposal for tentative API: server returns 202 + tentative_token. clients can poll /confirm or pass token in reads to get merge-aware responses. tentative entries GC after tenant-configured TTL (default 15s, strict tenants default 2s).
raj: we should avoid breaking existing clients. expose write_consistency flag at HTTP level: auto|tentative|strict. default auto -> runtime chooses tentative normally.
tom: metrics to add: tentative_emitted, tentative_confirmed, tentative_abandoned, epoch_mismatch_rejects, handoff_quiesce_ms. also per-tenant histograms for handoff latency.
emily: operator config sketch:
``nhand_off_policy: adaptive
adaptive:
  tentative_ttl_ms: 2000
  epoch_check: warn
  backlog_threshold: 2000
strict:
  tentative_ttl_ms: 200
  epoch_check: enforce
  global_sequencer: optional
``n
raj: long-term option: global sequencer for strict tenants to guarantee ordering. heavy refactor but worth for enterprise SLAs.
zara: add adaptive migration: if tenant sees >0.1% divergence in 1h, and breaches happen in 3 consecutive 10m windows, schedule manual migration to strict path. avoid automatic sequencer moves without human review.
emily: ops runbook note: default fallback on problematic handoff is tentative-write, but allow forced short read-only quiesce (up to 500ms) for emergency stabilization.
tom: SDK changes: helpers for handling 202 tentative responses, idempotency token usage, and confirm polling. docs must show retry/backoff patterns.
ops-bot: Action created: CAN-2026-400 - tentative-write canary (0.5% traffic)
emily: i'll open PR with epoch-stamping detection, tentative-write implementation, telemetry, and the canary plan. thanks all.
